about: Missions to Mars and its moons that are en route, launched recently, in development, proposed, or recently cancelled, as of 18 November 2026. Missions already operating at Mars (Perseverance, Curiosity, MRO, Mars Express, TGO, Tianwen-1, Hope, MAVEN, Odyssey) are out of scope except where they bear on a row. Dates are given as the sources state them. launch_earliest/latest and arrival_earliest/latest are editorial ranges built from the sources, not agency figures. Statements by company founders (Musk) are marked Proposed. Several 2026 developments come only from secondary news or aggregator sites, which is flagged per row in 'uncertain'. I found no new Mars mission from Japan beyond MMX, and nothing from the UAE beyond the long-term Mars 2117 goal. Roscosmos plans are paper concepts. Mars launch windows recur about every 26 months, so a mission announced for a year without a window (e.g. ISRO's '2030') will in practice use an adjacent window. launch_year, arrival_year and return_year are decimal years (2028.83 = November 2028) from the dates in launch and arrival; null where no target date exists. launch_earliest and launch_latest are the range drawn on the chart. slipped_years are the earlier target launch years named in earlier_targets.

windows.note: Wikipedia lists Nov-Dec. MMX used a window opening 19 Oct 2026 (JAXA window 19 Oct-7 Nov). ESCAPADE's powered Earth flybys (7 and 9 Nov 2026) used the same alignment.
Planned for Rosalind Franklin, Tianwen-3, SR-1 Freedom and Aeolus, and possibly the Mars Telecommunications Network.
Wikipedia assigns ISRO's Mars Lander Mission here.
No mission assigned. This is the year of China's first crewed flight in its 2021 roadmap.

missions.name: ESCAPADE
missions.launch: 13 Nov 2025 (New Glenn); trans-Mars powered Earth flybys 7 and 9 Nov 2026
missions.arrival: Mars orbit insertion planned 7 and 9 Sep 2027; science orbits by mid-2028
missions.agency: NASA (SIMPLEx); UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory (PI); Rocket Lab (spacecraft); Blue Origin (launch)
missions.goal: Two small orbiters measure from two vantage points at once how the solar wind strips Mars's atmosphere and shapes its magnetosphere.
missions.status_note: Launched Nov 2025 into a loiter orbit near Sun-Earth L2. Powered Earth flybys on 7 and 9 Nov 2026 put both spacecraft on a ~10-month cruise to Mars. The 11-month prime science mission is to start ~mid-2028, after the late-2027 solar conjunction.
missions.earlier_targets: 2022 (Psyche rideshare, dropped), Oct 2024 (New Glenn not ready)
missions.cost: USD 55M (2024): SIMPLEx cost cap excluding launch; final total not published
missions.uncertain: The exact 7/9 Sep 2027 orbit-insertion dates come from a secondary site (newspaceeconomy.ca). NASA's page says only that the two arrive a few days apart and must finish orbit adjustment before the late-2027 conjunction. The earlier slip history (2022 Psyche rideshare, Oct 2024) comes from general knowledge of the mission and was not re-fetched here.

missions.name: MMX
missions.launch: 19 Oct 2026 19:41 UTC (20 Oct JST), H3-24L from Tanegashima
missions.arrival: Mars orbit August 2027; Phobos quasi-satellite orbit about a month later
missions.agency: JAXA; partners CNES and DLR (IDEFIX rover), NASA (MEGANE spectrometer), ESA (ground stations, comms)
missions.goal: Orbit Mars, survey Phobos and Deimos, and land on Phobos to collect at least 10 g of regolith for return to Earth, testing whether the moons are captured asteroids or impact debris.
missions.status_note: Launched successfully on H3 flight 10 on 19/20 Oct 2026, and JAXA confirmed separation and the planned trajectory. Next steps: IDEFIX rover release on Phobos ~2028-2029, sampling 2029-2030, departure from Mars 2030, capsule landing at Woomera, Australia in 2031.
missions.uncertain: No post-launch health update after late Oct 2026 was found. Sources differ on when the rover is released (CNES: Dec 2028; Wikipedia: 2029). The return is given as 'JFY 2031' in some sources and '2031' in others. The 2024->2026 slip followed the March 2023 H3 failure.

missions.name: Rosalind Franklin rover
missions.agency: ESA; NASA (launch on Falcon Heavy, landing-platform braking engines, radioisotope heater units); Thales Alenia Space (prime); Airbus (landing platform)
missions.goal: Drill up to 2 m below the surface at Oxia Planum to look for signs of past life protected from radiation.
missions.status_note: ESA member states secured full ESA funding at the Nov 2025 Ministerial Council, and NASA selected Falcon Heavy on 16 Apr 2026. The White House FY2027 request (Apr 2026) includes no money for NASA's contribution. Congress has not finished FY2027 appropriations.
missions.cost: EUR 522M (2024): ESA contract to Thales Alenia Space (Apr 2024) for completing the mission; not total mission cost. One report puts the NASA launch contract at USD 175.7 million (unconfirmed).
missions.uncertain: If the US drops its contribution (launch, engines, RHUs), the launch would likely slip to the 2031 window while Europe develops replacements. launch_latest 2031 reflects that risk, not a date from a source. The 2018 and 2020 slips predate Russia's withdrawal in 2022.

missions.name: Tianwen-3
missions.launch: around 2028; two Long March 5 launches from Wenchang, window late 2028 - early 2029
missions.agency: CNSA (China National Space Administration); international payloads invited
missions.goal: Land on Mars, collect samples and return them to Earth; the search for traces of past life is the top science goal.
missions.status_note: Chief scientist Hou Zengqian said on 3 Sep 2026, at the Hefei deep-space conference, that the mission remains on track for a ~2028 launch and a ~2031 return.
missions.uncertain: The arrival year is inferred (about 7-11 months after a late-2028/early-2029 launch); CNSA does not state it. The schedule has moved earlier, not later: 2021 statements gave 'around 2030' for the sample return, and 2024 statements set a 2028 launch and 2031 return. Wikipedia gives a July 2031 return under an earlier plan.

missions.name: Mars Sample Return (NASA/ESA)
missions.launch: was planned for late 2020s; no date now
missions.agency: NASA (JPL) with ESA
missions.goal: Retrieve the rock cores Perseverance is caching in Jezero Crater and bring them to Earth.
missions.status_note: The FY2026 appropriations act, passed in Jan 2026 (joint explanatory statement 6 Jan 2026), gives $0 to the existing MSR program and says it 'does not support' it. The House's proposed $300M was dropped. Instead, $110M goes to a 'Mars Future Missions' line for technology that could support a later sample return.
missions.earlier_targets: return 2031, return 2033, return 2035-2039 (2025 options), return 2040 (2024 estimate)
missions.cost: USD 11B (2024): NASA April 2024 estimate (up from ~$7B), with return slipping to 2040; deemed unaffordable
missions.uncertain: Some outlets say the program was left unfunded rather than formally terminated. The slip list comes from general reporting on MSR's history (originally a ~2031 return, 2033 in the IRB era, 'up to 2040' in April 2024), and the intermediate dates vary by source. Rocket Lab pitched a ~$4B fixed-price alternative with a return by 2031; it was not selected.

missions.name: Earth Return Orbiter (ESA)
missions.agency: ESA; Airbus Defence and Space (prime)
missions.goal: Capture the sample container in Mars orbit and fly it back to Earth as part of MSR.
missions.status_note: After the 345th ESA Council (March 2026) the Director General said member states had asked for ERO's cancellation. ESA is negotiating with Airbus to reuse parts such as the electric propulsion, possibly in the proposed ZefERO mission.
missions.uncertain: No formal ESA Council decision text was found. What has been reported is a member-state request plus wind-down talks with Airbus.

missions.name: ZefERO
missions.agency: ESA (proposed, reusing Earth Return Orbiter hardware)
missions.goal: Build a European Mars orbiter from the cancelled ERO to study Martian winds and geology and act as a communications relay.
missions.status_note: ESA proposed it in 2026 after the ERO cancellation. It is not yet approved or funded.
missions.uncertain: The name, scope and 2032 date come from news reports, not from an ESA page I could read. 2032 falls between Mars windows (2031 and 2033), so the date is approximate.

missions.name: LightShip and SpotLight
missions.agency: ESA
missions.goal: Fly a solar-electric 'Mars tug' that carries small spacecraft to Mars and provides relay, with SpotLight, a low-altitude surface-imaging orbiter, as its first passenger.
missions.status_note: ESA lists LightShip as proposed; whether to start full development was due to be decided at the Nov 2025 Ministerial Council. ZefERO may take over its relay role.
missions.uncertain: I could not confirm whether CM25 (Nov 2025) approved development.

missions.name: Mars Telecommunications Network
missions.launch: orbiter to be delivered to NASA by 31 Dec 2028; reported launch 2028
missions.agency: NASA; Blue Origin (contract awarded, Blue Ring platform); protested by Rocket Lab
missions.goal: Place a commercial orbiter that provides high-rate communications and navigation for Mars surface and orbital missions through 2035 and for future human missions.
missions.status_note: The July 2025 reconciliation act (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, sec. 40005) provided $700M. NASA awarded Blue Origin a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $700M on 2 Sep 2026. Rocket Lab filed a GAO protest on 11 Sep 2026, and NASA suspended performance pending a decision.
missions.uncertain: No GAO ruling was found. GAO normally decides within 100 days of filing, i.e. by about 20 Dec 2026. If the protest is upheld, NASA would have to re-evaluate the bids, and the orbiter would likely miss the 2028 window. The suspension is reported by Forbes (page not readable here, 403) and was taken from search snippets.
missions.full_name: Mars Telecommunications Network (formerly Mars Telecommunications Orbiter)

missions.name: Aeolus
missions.agency: NASA (Ames: science payload) with Relativity Space (spacecraft, launch, operations)
missions.goal: Provide the first integrated, daily, global view of Martian winds, temperatures, dust and clouds, which also reduces risk for future landings.
missions.status_note: NASA Administrator Isaacman announced it at Relativity Space on 17 Jun 2026 as a public-private partnership, and NASA commits to at least one Martian year of science operations. The contract value has not been disclosed, and Relativity's Terran R has not flown.
missions.uncertain: Outlets differ on the instrument list: Engadget and The Register list four atmospheric instruments, and The Next Web also mentions a radar sounder. The arrival year is inferred from a 2028 launch. The funding level is unknown.

missions.name: SR-1 Freedom and Skyfall
missions.agency: NASA
missions.goal: Fly the first fission-powered interplanetary spacecraft, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion and delivering the Skyfall payload of Ingenuity-class helicopters to Mars.
missions.status_note: NASA announced it at its 'Ignition' event on 24 Mar 2026. It reuses hardware built for the Lunar Gateway. At the announcement it was undecided whether it flies by Mars or enters orbit.
missions.uncertain: Experts call the schedule very ambitious, and a draft MEPAG statement (2026) criticised the uncompeted Skyfall payload. No funding source or total cost was found.

missions.name: ISRO Mars Lander (Mangalyaan-2)
missions.agency: ISRO
missions.kind: Lander (orbiter + lander, possibly rover and helicopter)
missions.goal: Make India's first soft landing on Mars with an orbiter and a lander, possibly carrying a rover and a helicopter.
missions.status_note: ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said in Nov 2025 that it will launch in 2030. Reports conflict on whether the Union Cabinet has approved it; one says the government approved it on 22 Mar 2025 after the Space Commission endorsed it.
missions.uncertain: 2030 has no Mars launch window (windows are late 2028-early 2029 and early 2031), so '2030' probably means the early-2031 window. The earlier target years come from older listings and news and were never firm commitments.

missions.name: Starship to Mars, uncrewed
missions.launch: SpaceX site: cargo NET 2028; Musk (Feb 2026): Mars city work starts in 5-7 years
missions.agency: SpaceX
missions.goal: Land uncrewed Starships on Mars to test entry and landing and to pre-position cargo for later crews.
missions.status_note: No Starship launched to Mars in the late-2026 window. On 8 Feb 2026 Musk said SpaceX had shifted its focus to a 'self-growing city' on the Moon (per the WSJ, an uncrewed lunar landing targeted for Mar 2027) and that work on a Mars city would start in about 5-7 years. All dates are company aspirations.
missions.uncertain: The 'NET 2028' wording on SpaceX's Mars page is reported second-hand; I did not fetch spacex.com. Some secondary sources call 2029 'most likely'. The 5-7 year phrase refers to starting a Mars city, not to a first uncrewed launch.

missions.name: Starship to Mars, crewed
missions.launch: no current date; Sept 2024 statement: first crews 4 years after the 2026 uncrewed flights
missions.agency: SpaceX
missions.goal: Send people to Mars on Starship as the first step toward a self-sustaining city.
missions.status_note: Earlier crew targets (2028 or 2030) depended on uncrewed flights in 2026 that did not happen. Since the Feb 2026 Moon-first pivot there is no stated crewed Mars date.
missions.uncertain: launch_earliest/latest is an editorial range, not a SpaceX figure. The slip list reflects past Musk statements (crews in 2024 per 2016 talks; 2028/2030 per 2024-25 talks).

missions.name: NASA astronauts to Mars
missions.agency: NASA
missions.goal: Use Artemis and a lunar base as a proving ground, then send astronauts to Mars.
missions.status_note: There is no funded crewed Mars mission and no date. In March 2026 NASA prioritised a ~$20B lunar base built over seven years. Isaacman said crewed Mars missions could come before 2040 if lunar operations succeed. The Mars-relevant pieces now funded are SR-1 Freedom (nuclear propulsion) and the Mars Telecommunications Network.
missions.uncertain: I did not read NASA's Moon to Mars Architecture Definition Document directly. The 2010 'mid-2030s' goal in 'slipped' comes from general knowledge (Obama-era policy) and was not re-sourced here.
missions.full_name: NASA crewed Mars missions (Moon to Mars)

missions.name: China's astronauts to Mars
missions.agency: CNSA / CALT (China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology)
missions.goal: Fly crews to Mars and build a base, after robotic sample return and site selection.
missions.status_note: CALT head Wang Xiaojun presented the roadmap in June 2021, and no newer official schedule was found. Independent analysts called a 2033 crewed Mars-orbit mission infeasible before the late 2030s.
missions.uncertain: The roadmap is old (2021) and is not an approved programme. China's approved crewed goal is the Moon by 2030.

missions.name: Impulse/Relativity Mars lander
missions.agency: Impulse Space (lander), Relativity Space (Terran R launch)
missions.goal: Make the first commercial Mars landing with a propulsive lander and an InSight-derived heat shield.
missions.status_note: Announced in 2022 for 2024 and moved to 2026 in 2023. Nothing launched in 2026 and no update was found. Relativity, now led by Eric Schmidt, is building NASA's Aeolus orbiter instead.
missions.uncertain: Wikipedia's window table lists it under 2028/29 but cites an obsolete source. The project is probably dormant.
missions.full_name: Impulse Space / Relativity Space Mars lander

missions.name: Mars Life Explorer
missions.launch: no date; decadal survey: start after MSR spending peaks
missions.agency: NASA (decadal-survey concept)
missions.goal: Drill into mid-latitude ground ice to look for extant life and assess modern habitability.
missions.status_note: The 2023-2032 planetary decadal survey (2022) ranked it the top medium-class Mars mission after MSR. No NASA start was found as of 2026, and MEPAG warned in 2026 that current Mars plans do not follow decadal priorities.
missions.uncertain: This is a concept only. The decadal survey's cost estimate (roughly $1.2-2.2B) was not re-verified here.

missions.name: Boomerang (Phobos)
missions.agency: Roscosmos / Lavochkin
missions.goal: Return soil from Phobos as the first stage of the 'Expedition-M' Mars programme, retrying the failed 2011 Phobos-Grunt.
missions.status_note: Russian reporting in 2023 described it as a post-2030 plan. Anatoly Zak's RussianSpaceWeb schedule (Apr 2026) no longer lists any Russian Mars or Phobos probes.
missions.uncertain: This is a paper concept, and its funding is unknown.

missions.name: Mars 2117 (UAE)
missions.agency: UAE Government / Mohammed bin Rashid Space Centre
missions.goal: Build the first human settlement on Mars within 100 years, as a long-term national goal.
missions.status_note: Announced in Feb 2017. The UAE's near-term missions are the Hope orbiter (at Mars since 2021), lunar work and the Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt. No new UAE Mars spacecraft has been announced.
missions.uncertain: This is an aspiration with no mission design.
